docs.syntax: In a criterion, ? matches one character and * matches any run of them
docs.explain:
A criterion is the text that tells COUNTIF or SUMIF which rows count, and two marks inside it act as wildcards. A question mark stands for exactly one character, a star for any run of them including none. Quoted, they turn a plain criterion into a pattern.

On this sheet the region column holds whole words, so Nor* counts the three North rows and N* counts the same three. The code column is where patterns do real work. Every code is two letters, a hyphen and four digits, so ??-* matches all four, and the amounts come to 460.

The criterion always travels in quotes. Without them Excel reads Nor as a name and no count comes back. COUNTIF and SUMIF read criteria the same way, so one pattern serves both.

errors.text: The criterion cannot be read as text or as a comparison, usually because its quotes are unbalanced.
A range points at rows that no longer exist after a column was deleted.
COUNTIF(B2:B5,"N") matches nothing, and 0 looks like a real answer on the page.

docs.atWork: Counting or totalling the rows whose code or name fits one pattern.
docs.outcome: Write a wildcard criterion in COUNTIF and reuse the same pattern in SUMIF.
docs.teaches: ? and * inside a criteria string, and the same pattern driving a count and a sum
docs.dataset: Regions and amounts beside codes that share one pattern

screens.prompt: In D2, count the North rows with a wildcard criterion.

hints.syntax: =COUNTIF(B2:B5,"Nor*"): the region column, then the pattern in quotes.
hints.func-countif: Counting rows that fit a pattern is COUNTIF's own job.
hints.value: Three regions start with Nor: rows 2, 4 and 5.
hints.error: A pattern that also catches South gives 4, and the grader expects 3.

reject.why: every region counts the same, which is not what a criterion asks
the amounts are added rather than the North rows counted
no region is the single letter N
the last North row is outside the range
one row starts with S, not three
the region column is never read
the count is then divided by zero
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D2, add the amounts of every code that fits the two-letter pattern with a wildcard.

hints.syntax: =SUMIF(A2:A5,"??-*",C2:C5): the code column, the pattern, then the amounts.
hints.func-sumif: A total that depends on a pattern is SUMIF's job.
hints.value: All four codes are two letters, a hyphen and four digits, so all four amounts count.
hints.error: A pattern of *1* keeps three codes and totals 380, because BO-2299 has no 1 in it.

reject.why: the pattern never enters the formula
the codes are counted rather than the amounts added
only the rows whose digits hold a one are added
the last code is outside the range
the sum range holds regions rather than amounts
the code column is never read
the total is then divided by zero
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

seo.title: Wildcards in Excel criteria
seo.description: A question mark stands in for one character, a star for any run of them. Nor*, N* and North all select the same rows, because a criterion is a pattern.
